Instead, Glave tackled 2026 with an intensive determination to succeed. So much so that even when doubts, nerves or physical issues crept in he was able to channel them out.

It was notable watching the start line to the 100m final just how relaxed Glave appeared, a state very difficult to achieve ahead of an event that means so much and that he would have worked so hard towards. But this was an athlete totally in flow.

"I would say I came into this season just to show a bit of redemption after the loss of years, loss of seasons to injury," Glave says.

"But to also start this season with a very resilient mindset of: 'I want to go for everything.' I was a 2024 bronze medallist at the European Championships and missed the gold medal by a small margin. So why not dream bigger and upgrade my medal to gold?

"That was the aim and objective for the season, from the start of the season. To be European champion and to be able to walk away from from that 100m being crowned king of Europe. It's an amazing feeling.

"It brings me calmness. I've been dreaming of this moment and to be able to live it, it's very surreal.

"Over the last few days, I have had discomfort in my abdominal muscles, but I was not going to let that stop me from obtaining my objective.

"I was able to go out there, regardless of how I was feeling, the discomfort I was enduring, and just focus on the job that was presented in front of me. I got the job done.

"I was ready for this moment, this occasion. I was ready mentally, most importantly, regardless of how I was feeling emotionally or physically, I wasn't going to let that take away the moment from me because I prepared all season long for it.

"This season was all about redemption, that's the theme, and speaking to my sports psychologist, we've been working on all of those formulas to make sure I'm preparing the best way possible to get through."

'2024 back injury left a void in my heart'

Thinking back, Glave lays bare the inner turmoil he experienced having battled through one serious back injury, won a European Championship bronze, but then suffered with his back again to miss an Olympics Games and virtually have to start his career all over again.

"It was very disappointing. After the 2024 European Championships, I could feel I was on that momentum, because the trials were two weeks afterwards.

"My first session back after I was crowned European bronze medallist, I picked up the injury and it was a very sad moment for me. My mind went to missing the Olympics, because everyone trains towards going to that.

"And to get a European bronze and have that momentum going into the Olympics, that's what everyone wants. To cut the journey short at that moment, it left a a void in my heart. I'm never going to get that moment back, that's gone."

One man Glave has repeatedly singled out in the aftermath of his success has been coach Michael Afilaka, someone he describes as more than just his sprint coach: "a mentor, life coach, a man of wisdom and integrity."

Indeed, referencing his working relationship with Afilaka from serious injury to European champion proves very emotional for Glave.

"He's been doing this for over 20 years and is a private person, but God presented him to me on this journey. Having him beside me has been a life-changing decision.

"During those darkest times of my life, he's the only that is there. His belief, his dedication to continue to show up for me, I haven't really seen that before. I haven't really seen it in my life, in the way he has shown up.

"It's very emotional just talking about it every time, because he didn't have to do it, but because of his persona, he wants the best for me."

'The next goal is world domination'

In terms of what's next, Glave is clear. He wants to challenge on a world level at the top of the sport.

"World domination is now the main goal, but just to have this stepping stone as European champion, I'm focusing on one step at a time.

"This season is like a stepping stone of what is to come for Romell Glave. I'm in a historic British team and now have the ultimate chance as well.

"So to be there and show up in a field of world-class athletes, that's the main objective now. To perform against those athletes, the world's best."

articles.title: European Athletics Championship: Keely Hodgkinson forced to settle for silver as Audrey Werro wins women's 800m gold
articles.summary: Swiss favourite Audrey Werro holds off Keely Hodgkinson to clinch women's 800m gold at European Athletics Championship in Birmingham; result ended British Olympic champion Hodgkinson's hopes of a hat-trick of European 800m victories, having clinched gold in Munich 2022 and Rome 2024
articles.body:
Keely Hodgkinson came up just short of a coveted European 800m title hat-trick after Swiss favourite Audrey Werro won their hotly-anticipated showdown in Birmingham as the British Olympic champion settled for silver.

Hodgkinson started quicker but was overtaken by Werro on the back straight and the latter was never overtaken after the first 200m.

Double-defending champion Hodgkinson was just behind as they rounded the final bend, but Werro would not be caught and crossed the finish in a championship record 1:54.81.

  • Glave: From 2022 in a back brace to European champion - 'Delayed but not denied'
  • European Athletics Championships 2026: Updates from Birmingham
  • England finish second in Commonwealth Games medal table
  • 'Ramsay-Peaty emotion showed what Commonwealth Games means'

Hodgkinson claimed silver in 1:55.01 and the Netherlands' Femke-Broeders Bol took bronze in a national record 1:55.54.

After losing her title, Hodgkinson said: "Mixed emotions. With that level of competition, any medal is an achievement.

"I thought I was going to win. I didn't do anything wrong, just one of those things.

"I've had a pretty good day today, just didn't go the way that I wanted.

"There were so many different ways that could have played out and we'd figure it out after the first 100m. Audrey wanted to take it on and with that wind I was happy to let her. We're all really great athletes so I knew it was going to be close. I'm looking forward to the next match-up.

"I've said all year it's really motivating to be in such a competitive event. I love it, it brings out the best in me. Championship racing, that's what it's all about, you don't know how it's going to go and some people can have a good day or a bad day. I had a pretty good day today but it just didn't go how I wanted it to."

The world record remains the longest-standing record in athletics set in 1983 by Jarmila Kratochvilova's with a time of 1:53.28 seconds.

While the world record wasn't troubled, Werro's time of 1:54.81 did break the championship record set by Olga Mineyeva in 1982.

Hodgkinson's silver medal is Britain's 10th medal in five days on home soil. Earlier on Friday, Zharnel Hughes claimed silver in the men's 200m.

articles.title: 2 College Cyclists Killed and 7 Injured In Tennessee Car Crash
articles.summary: HAMPTON, Tenn. (AP) — Two members of a university cycling team were killed and seven others were injured Wednesday when a car collided with a group of riders in northeastern Tennessee, state officials said.
articles.body:
HAMPTON, Tenn. (AP) — Two members of a university cycling team were killed and seven others were injured Wednesday when a car collided with a group of riders in northeastern Tennessee, state officials said.

Milligan University, a private Christian school with just over 1,200 students, said 11 of its cyclists were out together on a morning training ride when they were struck by a driver in Hampton, about 11 miles (18 kilometers) from the campus in the foothills of the Appalachian Mountains.

The county's district attorney, Steve Finney, said a 69-year-old man from North Carolina had been arrested and faced two counts of reckless vehicular homicide and five counts of aggravated assault by vehicle with recklessness.

York Responded to Ad on Prostitution Site Before Arrest

Milligan sophomores Haylan Engdahl, of Winthrop Harbor, Illinois, and Brayden Rogers, of Huntsville, Alabama, were killed in the crash, university President Stephen Waers said. The other student-athletes were transported to the nearby Johnson City Medical Center, he said.

"We need to help our brothers and sisters bear burdens that are too great for any one person to carry alone," Waers said in an emotional video message shared with the school community. He urged students to come together in prayer for their injured peers.

As of Wednesday evening, four students were in critical condition, two others were stable but remained in the hospital, and one student had been discharged, said the hospital's trauma medical director, Dr. Bracken Burns.

Earlier this year, the Milligan University men's cycling team won a team time trial national championship at the USA Cycling Collegiate Road Nationals in Wisconsin.

The Tennessee Highway Patrol was still investigating the circumstances of the crash, said Maj. Roy Brown. The speed limit on the section of Highway 19 where the the crash occurred is 50 miles per hour (about 80 kilometers per hour), officials said.

articles.title: Robot Breaks Usain Bolt's 100m Record on Video at Olympics-like World Humanoid Robot Games in China
articles.summary: It took 17 years to find anything in the world that can run the 100 meters faster than Usain Bolt, but a humanoid robot created in China finally did it.
articles.body:
It took 17 years to find anything in the world that can run the 100 meters faster than Usain Bolt, but a humanoid robot created in China finally did it.

A humanoid robot ran the 100 meters in 9.39 seconds at the World Humanoid Robot Games on Saturday, breaking the human world record of 9.58 seconds set by Bolt at the 2009 World Championships.

That wasn't the only time one of the robots surpassed a world record set by a human.

Per Achmad Ibrahim and Chan Ho-Him of the Associated Press, a humanoid robot hit 2.88 meters in the standing high jump. The human record is 2.45 meters set by Cuba's Javier Sotomayor in 1993.

Ibrahim and Ho-Him noted both of the robots that broke the records are from X-Humanoid, which is based in Beijing.

The World Humanoid Robot Games are an Olympic-like event featuring humanoid robots. Saturday marks the first day of the 2026 Games, which are scheduled to run through Aug. 26.

After having more than 280 teams from various universities and private companies in 2025, the field has expanded significantly this with 666 teams and 2,056 robots competing.

There are 30 competitive sporting events taking place over the five days. Track and field, dance, wushu and gymnastics are among the disciplines in the competition.

articles.title: Usain Bolt: From sprint stardom to Sunday league - athletics icon set for Wythenshawe Vets bow
articles.summary: Former sprinter Usain Bolt - who won eight gold medals across three Olympics - will return to the football pitch for Manchester side Wythenshawe Vets
articles.body:
Usain Bolt is registered to play for a Sunday league team in Manchester, with the Olympic champion set to make another foray into football.

The former sprint star, who still holds the world records for the 100m and 200m, has appeared on the squad list for Wythenshawe FC Veterans over-35s on the Football Association Full-Time website.

The team play in the Cheshire Veterans League, and feature a side made up of former top-level professionals.

  • England finish second in Commonwealth Games medal table
  • 'Ramsay-Peaty emotion showed what Commonwealth Games means'

Managed by former Manchester City and Republic of Ireland midfielder Stephen Ireland, the line-up also includes Danny Drinkwater, Antonio Valencia, Joleon Lescott, Emile Heskey, Marc Albrighton and Papiss Cisse.

Bolt, 40, is a major football fan, and has harboured an ambition to build a professional career in the sport since retiring following the World Championships in 2017.

His athletic career saw him win eight gold medals across three Olympics, and skyrocket to global fame.

The Jamaican became known for his trademark victory pose.

The star filed a patent application for the distinctive stance to market a range of products including sunglasses, jewellery, hats and sporting goods.

He briefly played for the Australian A-League team Central Coast Mariners.

The Manchester United supporter has also been a regular participant in Soccer Aid charity matches over the last decade.

He has also trained with other clubs across the world, most notably German heavyweights Borussia Dortmund.

Wythenshawe, yet to announce Bolt's signing, have been contacted for comment.

articles.title: Ethiopia's Yomif Kejelcha breaks men's half marathon world record
articles.summary: Ethiopia's Yomif Kejelcha breaks the men's half marathon world record in a time of  56 minutes 51 seconds in a World Athletics road race in Buenos Aires.
articles.body:
Ethiopia's Yomif Kejelcha has broken the men's half marathon world record, winning a World Athletics road race in Buenos Aires on Sunday in 56 minutes 51 seconds.

The 29-year-old previously held the record with a time of 57:30, set in Valencia in October 2024, but lost that to Uganda's Jacob Kiplimo in March .

Kiplimo ran 57:20 in Lisbon earlier this year but Kejelcha has now knocked 29 seconds off that time to regain the record, subject to official ratification.

The world track silver medallist in the 10,000m also holds the world record for a men's 10,000m road race.

He also became one of the first men to run a sub-two hour marathon in record-eligible conditions earlier this year when finishing second behind Kenya's Sebastian Sawe in the London Marathon.

Sawe won the record-breaking race in 1:59:30 , beating Kejelcha by just 11 seconds.

articles.summary: Hockey News: NEW DELHI: Indiaâs women hockey players have made an emotional appeal to save the Womenâs Hockey India League (HIL), insisting that the competition ha.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indiaâs women hockey players have made an emotional appeal to save the Womenâs Hockey India League (HIL), insisting that the competition has played a crucial role in building the confidence of a young side that is on the brink of its best-ever World Cup finish since 1974.With 11 World Cup debutants in the squad, India have suffered only one defeat against Olympic champions the Netherlands and held Olympic silver medallists China to a 2-2 draw in their opening match. A goalless draw against Australia ended their hopes of reaching the semifinals, but India will now play for fifth and sixth place â a finish that would still be their best at the World Cup in 52 years.The players believe the Women's HIL has been central to their progress and fear its discontinuation could damage the pathway for the next generation.âHIL has benefited us a lotâVeteran midfielder Neha, who led Odisha Warriors to the inaugural HIL title in the 2024-25 season, stressed the importance of the league in giving young players access to a higher level of competition.âI think we have done our best to inspire girls in India to hold a hockey stick. People prefer their kids to play individual sports, but this should give them hope,â Neha told PTI.âIn the last two years, HIL for women has benefited us a lot. Junior and senior Nationals do not have this level of competition. Women's HIL has given us players like Baljeet, Sakshi and Rutuja, who are part of this World Cup team. For upcoming players also, we need this league. It should not be discontinued.âSalima Tete highlights talent pathwayCaptain Salima Tete also underlined how the league has helped widen India's talent pool and given emerging players a route into the national setup.âWe have many players from HIL in the Indian team. They get a chance to be selected for the national camp, which is an important opportunity for them,â she said.âThis is just the beginning for us and there is much more to achieve. For that, HIL is a must so that our talent pool is broadened and the girls get good exposure to handling the pressure of international hockey.ââHIL has given me confidenceâSakshi Rana, another player who has benefited from the league, said the experience of playing alongside established international stars helped her handle pressure on the biggest stage.âHIL has given me confidence, which was very useful in this tournament. It is about handling pressure. We have played alongside many veteran players like World Cup top scorer Yibbi Janssen and learnt a lot,â she said.Navneet Kaur said the league also helped younger players overcome the fear of facing established international stars.âWe have been playing HIL for the last two years and gained confidence from that. We have played with some of the biggest names in international hockey and after sharing the dressing room with them, the fear and hesitation was gone,â she said.âThat gave us self-belief. We often discuss that they are like us and we can beat them because we have played with them.âNavneet urges corporate sector to step inNavneet also urged franchises and corporate houses to step in as the women's league faces financial uncertainty.âWe have heard that a few teams are pulling out of the Women's HIL, but at a time when our performance graph is going up, we want to request them to support us. It will be a big setback for women's hockey and the future crop of players,â she said.âI request the Sports Ministry and Hockey India to save this league. I also request the corporate sector, which invests huge money in cricket, to support women's hockey.âOur league does not require that much money. It is not about money, we need exposure. articles.standfirst: Radnaa Tseren, de Mongolia, se impone en la final de la distancia en categoría M90
articles.summary: Radnaa Tseren, de Mongolia, se impone en la final de la distancia en categoría M90
articles.body: En 1962 Radnaa Tseren ingresó en el Instituto Nacional de Educación Física de Mongolia y ahí empezó a correr. Pocos años después, en 1966 y tras graduarse en la Universidad, comenzó a participar en carreras de corta y media distancia. Han pasado 60 años desde entonces y Radnaa Tseren sigue corriendo. "Corro de 3 a 4 kilómetros todas las mañanas", decía el pasado año en una recepción con el presidente de Mongolia, Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh antes de proclamarse campeón del mundo Máster de 800 metros, en Florida. Pero Tseren no ha perdido velocidad y también disputa pruebas más explosivas, en las que igualmente sube al podio. Así, a sus 92 años, se ha proclamado campeón del mundo Máster de 100 metros en el evento de la categoría, que se está disputando en Daegu, tras ganar la final con un tiempo de 18.29, con +0.5 m/s de viento a favor. Lo hizo en la categoría de más de 90 años.

articles.title: Habrá duelo entre Ingebrigtsen y Kerr en el 1.500 del Ultimate de Budapest
articles.standfirst: Ambos atletas volverá a coincidir en una carrera... dos años después
articles.summary: Ambos atletas volverá a coincidir en una carrera... dos años después
articles.body: Habrá duelo entre Josh Kerr y Jakob Ingebrigtsen en el 1.500... dos años después. Será en el World Athletics Ultimate Championship, la nueva competición que se disputará en Budapest del 11 al 13 de septiembre. Para ello World Athletics ha contravenido sus propias normas, ya que solo podía conceder una invitación excepcional por disciplina y en este caso ha otorgado dos. Ambos atletas se medirán por primera vez desde la Liga de Diamante de Zúrich de 2024. El noruego, que sí tenía invitación automática para los 5000 metros como vigente campeón olímpico de la prueba, competirá en ambas distancias.  Tras sumar en Birmingham su cuarto oro continental consecutivo, en una temporada en la que apenas ha competido por los problemas físicos que arrastraba, Ingebrigtsen criticó la ausencia del británico en la cita continental, pese a que batió el récord del mundo de la milla y compitió en los Juegos de la Commonwealth. “Tenemos estos campeonatos por una razón y es para que los mejores atletas compitan”, dijo el noruego. “Creo que se está arruinando el deporte si no participamos”.  Por eso, Jakob aseguró con vistas al Ultimate que “me encanta competir y trato de hacerlo siempre que puedo”. Por su parte, Kerr afirmó que “esta temporada he tomado algunas decisiones que han dado mucho de qué hablar, pero siempre he querido demostrar mi valía en las carreras contra los mejores del mundo”. También el medallista de oro mundial y olímpico Gianmarco Tamberi fue confirmado para la prueba de altura. El italiano ganó recientemente su cuarto título en el Campeonato Europeo, con una marca de 2,32 m en Birmingham.

articles.title: Olympic hero Alysa Liu to sit out figure skating season before 2027 return
articles.summary: Olympic champion Alysa Liu will sit out the 2026-27 figure skating season, taking another break from competition while continuing to train ahead of a planned...
articles.body:
Olympic champion Alysa Liu will sit out the 2026-27 figure skating season, taking another break from competition while continuing to train ahead of a planned return the following year.

The 21-year-old American announced her decision on social media , saying she wanted time to "recalibrate" and develop her skating away from the demands of competition.

"I always want to challenge myself in new ways, so my artistry and skating can evolve," Liu wrote. "It's important to me that my sport reflects my personal growth."

Liu told NBC Sports that she intends to continue working with her longtime Bay Area coaches, Phillip DiGuglielmo and Massimo Scali, with an emphasis on her "overall artistry, spins, jumps, everything".

"I really want to improve my skating, and I wanted to take the time to do that for myself and just to evolve," she said. "And then I'll be back after that is done."

The decision represents another unconventional turn in a career that has carried Liu from child prodigy to burnout, retirement and an unlikely return as world and Olympic champion.

Related: 'She is our hero': Oakland celebrates Alysa Liu after Olympics triumph

Liu became the youngest ever US women's champion aged 13, when her 4ft 6in frame left her too short to reach the top of the podium without help from the other medalists. But the relentless training and attention that accompanied her rapid ascent gradually drained her enthusiasm for the sport.

She retired at 16, only months after finishing sixth in her Olympic debut at the 2022 Beijing Games, and later described how comprehensively she had come to reject the life built around her skating.

"I really hated skating when I quit," Liu said in the run-up to the Milano Cortina Olympics. "I didn't care about competitions. I didn't care about places. I didn't care about skaters. I didn't care about my programs. I just wanted to get away."

Liu enrolled at UCLA, studied psychology and went hiking in the Himalayas with friends while discovering an identity beyond the rink. Her desire to skate returned unexpectedly during a ski trip to Lake Tahoe, where gliding down the mountain rekindled her love of movement.

She began skating once a week at public sessions in El Segundo, California, and found that the difficult jumps that had propelled her childhood rise had not entirely deserted her. Liu eventually decided to mount a comeback, but only with greater control over her career, including her music, costumes, diet and training schedule.

The results would no longer define the experience, she insisted. Her initial ambition was simply to make another Olympic team and use the sport as a form of self-expression.

That approach carried Liu to a surprise world championship in 2025, making her the first American woman to win the title since Kimmie Meissner in 2006. In February, she landed seven clean triple jumps to rise from third place after the short program and win the Olympic women's singles title in Milan .

The West Oakland native became the first American woman to claim the event since Sarah Hughes in 2002. She also won gold in the Olympic team competition .

"Really the only word that comes to mind when I think about my entire journey is grateful," Liu told NBC Sports. "I think the reason why it's been so fun is because I have my own agency. I really like to skate, and so that's why I skate."

Liu said she assessed her emotional and physical state earlier this summer and concluded that stepping away was the right choice. DiGuglielmo and Scali supported the decision.

"Logically and emotionally and physically, this just makes the most sense," she told NBC Sports. "I will miss seeing the international competitors at all the international competitions, but there will be more, so it's fine."

A rush of opportunities followed Liu's Olympic victory. Nearly 5,000 people turned out for a homecoming celebration in her honor, where Oakland mayor Barbara Lee presented her with a key to the city. She withdrew from the world championships in March, performed alongside her Olympic teammates on the Stars on Ice tour, attended Louis Vuitton's Paris Fashion Week show and wore the label to the Met Gala .

Liu had been scheduled to compete at Skate America from 13-15 November in Everett, Washington.

articles.title: Olympic gold medalist Alysa Liu is taking the season off from figure skating
articles.summary: Liu has left the sport once before. This time, she vowed that she'll be back.
articles.body:
After a whirlwind in the aftermath of her spectacular Olympic gold-medal run, Alysa Liu isn't ready to get back to the grind.

Liu announced Tuesday that she's taking the 2026-27 season off from figure skating. The 21-year-old, who dazzled en route to team and individual gold at the Milano-Cortina Games in February, announced her plan on Instagram.

"To my supporters, While people are announcing programs, imma take this time to announce that I will not be competing this season. I always want to challenge myself in new ways, so my artistry & skating can evolve. It's important to me that my sport reflects my personal growth. I'm gonna take the time to recalibrate, fine-tune things & whatnot."

While people are announcing programs, imma take this time to announce that I will not be competing this season. I always want to challenge myself in new ways, so my artistry & skating can evolve. It's important to me that my sport reflects my personal growth. I'm gonna take the time to recalibrate, fine-tune things & whatnot."

This marks Liu's second notable break from figure skating. She retired at 16 years old after finishing seventh at the 2022 Olympics, only to return to the sport in time for her gold-medal run this year.

But don't worry, Liu fans. She vowed Tuesday that she'll be back.

"So fear not, I'll be back, & in the meantime I'll be rooting for my teammates near & far," she wrote. "See yall soon!!"

Liu became the first U.S. woman to win individual figure skating gold since Sarah Hughes in 2002.

Her victory, along with her fearless, carefree approach and unmistakable style, made her a global sensation, and she has been in high demand since. Her plate has been full away from the ice.

Liu did not skate in the World Championships in March, which took place just two months after the conclusion of the Olympics. She did skate this spring in the considerably more laid-back Stars on Ice exhibition Ice tour. And it wasn't clear until Tuesday that she intended to take next season off from the sport.

In fact, Liu told USA Today in May : "I really want to compete next season."

"While people are announcing programs, imma take this time to announce that I will not be competing this season," Liu wrote. "I always want to challenge myself in new ways, so my artistry & skating can evolve."

She explained that "it's important" to her that her competition reflects her "personal growth," and she'll take time away "to recalibrate" and "fine-tune things."

Liu reassured fans that she will return for the 2027-28 season, writing, "So fear not, I'll be back, & in the meantime I'll be rooting for my teammates near & far. See yall soon!!"

She opened up about her decision in an interview with NBC Sports , elaborating that she plans to focus on her "overall artistry," from spins and jumps, and more.

"I really want to improve my skating, and I wanted to take the time to do that for myself and just to evolve, and then I'll be back after that is done," Liu told the outlet in the article published Tuesday, adding that she plans to continue cheering on her teammates.

"Logically and emotionally and physically, this just makes the most sense," she said, later adding, "I just felt this was right. So I'm trusting my instincts."

The Olympian noted that she spoke with her coaches Phillip DiGuglielmo and Massimo Scali about the decision.

"I came to them, and they totally understood where I was coming from," Liu told NBC Sports. "I did have to explain a little bit, but they didn't think I needed to justify my reason for it or anything. So it was really chill."

She confessed that while she'll miss seeing the international competitors at all the international competitions, she'll be coming back and knows there will be more in the future.

Liu's Olympic teammates, gold medalists Ilia Malinin and Amber Glenn , will return to compete for the U.S. for the 2026-27 season, along with Olympic bronze medalist Jason Brown and pairs Alisa Efimova and Misha Mitrofanov and Emilea Zingas and Vadym Kolesnik .

Liu's announcement comes over a month after she won the ESPY for Best Breakthrough Athlete on July 15. The other nominees were Patriots quarterback Drake Maye , Las Vegas Raiders rookie Fernando Mendoza and San Jose Sharks' Macklin Celebrini .

During her acceptance speech, Liu touched on her career in the sport, which began at 5 years old.

"I had some really rough times in it, I took two years off," she said. "So, for me, this really feels like I broke through in my own way, for myself, and for my sport."

"My goal is always to share my story and to connect with people," Liu told PEOPLE after her historic victories. "To have my experiences, turn them into a performance, and have my emotions be a part of that and get people to feel something."

articles.title: Athletics 4, Twins 2: Bats go cold
articles.summary: Taj Bradley threw an immaculate inning, and Byron Buxton hurt his hip again, because we can’t have nice things.
articles.body:
The A's jumped out to an early lead in the 2nd inning when Carlos Cortes smacked a 2-run homer to right. Fast forward to the 5th, with the Twins offense still struggling against lefty rookie Gage Jump, Taj threw 9 pitches and all of them were strikes for the first immaculate inning in Twins history. This was surprising to me, I figured Johan Santana or somebody must have done it before, but I guess not.

Things were still looking great for Taj two outs into the 6th inning, but a single by Lawrence Butler , an RBI double by Tommy White, and an RBI single by Donovan Walton pushed their lead to 4 runs.

The one hit the Twins had in the first 6 innings against Jump was a pop up that landed 5 feet from the pitcher's mound in the 4th. I'm not sure how this is considered a hit, but it does help Royce Lewis ' batting average, I guess. In the top of the 7th, Royce got himself a "real" hit with a line drive to left. One out later, Kaelen Culpepper doubled to bring in the Twins first run. Then a Brooks Lee double put two in scoring position for Victor Caratini , who grounded out for an RBI to make it a 2-4 game. The final chance for the Twins tonight came with 2 on and 2 out for Luke Keaschall , but he struck out looking to end the threat.

To add injury to insult, Buxton had to leave the game after appearing to aggravate his hip chasing down a ball in the gap in the 7th inning.

In the standings, the Twins sit at 64-69 and may fall to 3 games back in the wild card hunt. Also, the Royals have won 9 straight somehow.

Taj Bradley : 6.2 IP, 7 H, 4 ER, BB, 11 K, Immaculate inning

Four hits as a team just isn't gonna cut it usually, and it definitely didn't tonight.
